item.title: Pandas - Appending Cost
item.description:
For Robotics and Data Science projects i use Pandas for data collect and storage. Especially, for collecting live data from simulators for Behavior Cloning (BC), Pandas is handy for its consistency.

During data collection, each data from simulator can be either appended to a existing list or dataframe which will be saved at the end. For multiple sensor data Pandas will be prefered over list due to multi-column insertion.

# Code simulating contiguous memory
import pandas as pd
import time
num_cols = 5000 # Increasing this makes the "copy" operation much heavier
df = pd.DataFrame(columns=[f'c{i}' for i in range(num_cols)])
# This loop slows down gradually
for i in range(2500):
start = time.time()
df.loc[len(df)] = [1.1] * num_cols
print(f"Row {i}: {time.time() - start}s")

Well everything might look good unless the data collection loop runs for 2000 iterations or more. Yes. That’s the breaking point. Technically, nothing is broken. Just your computer slows down (1 row insertion takes 3 seconds or more and increases) which is alot.

Its not your computer limitation or problem will Python. Just wrong function selection for the use case. We are dealing will DataFrame Fragmentation problem or Contiguous memory.

To understand this better, you need to know how computers store data. Contiguous memory means data is stored in one single, unbroken block in the computer’s RAM (like a row of houses with no gaps).

Pandas uses this method because it makes reading data very fast. However, it makes adding data very slow.

In my case, when you i use .loc to add a new row to a DataFrame, Pandas cannot simply “attach” the data to the end of the existing block. Usually, the space next to that block is already being used by other data.

To keep the memory contiguous, Pandas must:

Find a new, empty area of memory that is large enough for the entire new DataFrame.
Copy every single old row into this new area.
Add the new row at the end.

As your loop runs, the DataFrame gets bigger. This means the computer spends more and more time copying data. If you have N rows, the time it takes grows at a rate of N² (Quadratic Time). This is why the loop over 2,000 iteration or more will be much slower.

The slow down time increases gradually. But, no issues with 300 or 500 steps. Beyond that you can watch a movie.

The best way to solve this issue is to avoid using a DataFrame until the very end. Instead, use a Python List.

Python Lists are designed to grow. They do not require a full copy of the data every time a new data item is added. Adding an item to a list is a Constant Time operation (O(1)), meaning it stays fast no matter how big the list is.

Then do Batch Construction. All collected in the list first will be converted as DataFrame once. This way i have reduced the data collection time.

# Solution for contiguous memory
import pandas as pd
import time
num_cols = 5000 # Increasing this makes the "copy" operation much heavier
data_buffer = [] # list to store data
# This loop stays fast from start to finish
for i in range(2500):
start = time.time()
# Appending to a list is O(1)
data_buffer.append([1.1] * num_cols)
print(f"Row {i}: {time.time() - start}s")
# Creating the DataFrame at the end is O(N)
df = pd.DataFrame(data_buffer, columns=[f'c{i}' for i in range(num_cols)])

Hope will be helpful for someone like me. Learned this hard way.

Thanks for Reading.
